sources.entry: How to Hire a Product Manager

summary.title: How to Hire a Product Manager
summary.one_liner: Ken Norton's classic essay lays out six traits to look for when hiring a product manager, with sample interview questions for each.
keywords: how to hire a product manager
what makes a great product manager
takeaways: Prioritize raw intelligence and problem-solving ability over years of experience when hiring a PM.
Technical backgrounds help PMs work with engineers, but former engineers must stop making technical decisions themselves.
Product instinct can be tuned but not taught; evaluate it by checking whether a candidate echoes your product concerns, teaches you something, or surfaces interesting products.
Have representatives from engineering, design, marketing, sales and others interview the candidate, since PMs must channel many viewpoints.
Favor candidates who have shipped a product from concept to launch; later updates say to avoid brainteasers and favor work samples.
summary.summary: Ken Norton, a former engineer and Yahoo! Search product leader, presents an essay on what to look for in product managers and how product management differs from other roles. It is organized into six hiring criteria: raw intelligence, a strong technical background, product instincts, earned leadership, the ability to channel multiple viewpoints, and having shipped a product. Each section includes example interview questions and tips on references and interview panels. The essay was first published in 2005, and the page notes updates from 2023 that revise its stance on brainteasers and add design to the interview loop.
